## What this is

The follow-on to #1959: the highest-value defect that audit surfaced, plus a root-cause pass over the mistakes made *while* doing it.

## 1 — #xzitlr9: the dispatcher bypassed three declared operations

`parallel-execute.workflow.js` builds agent prompts naming raw homes, so **every dispatched batch skipped the guards those operations own** — unattended, in the delivery path that runs most often. Invisible until #1959 taught the #3224 scan to read workflow scripts as well as markdown.

**Rewired (2 of 6):**

| Site | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `:423` | `backlog.mjs scaffold … --blocked-by=` | `run.mjs scaffold … --blockedBy=` |
| `:452` | `backlog.mjs resolve <NNN> --graduated-to=` | `run.mjs resolve --ref=<NNN> --graduatedTo=` |

Both needed the flag-spelling flip: the operations parse camelCase, the raw CLIs kebab-case, and the parser is case-sensitive (#3253) — a copied kebab flag is refused as unknown. The resolve prompt now says so inline, since the agent reading it is the one who'd hit it.

**Not rewired — four `pr-land.mjs` sites, and this is a finding, not a shortfall.** `open-pr` declares neither `manifestFile` nor `repo`, and these calls need both: `--manifest-file` carries the couple manifest that *is* #2387's impl-first ordering, and `--repo` is how a sibling repo's PR opens at all. Rewiring would drop the manifest and break cross-repo PRs — a functional regression dressed as compliance. Each carries a reasoned `@operation-home-ok` marker naming exactly what is missing.

That is the same judgement `declared-homes.mjs` records for withholding `open-pr`'s own entry twice: *"an entry would have emitted six findings whose only honest answer was six exemption markers — a gate reporting a gap nobody could close."* The unblocking work is giving `open-pr` those two inputs.

**Verified:** six `undelegated raw home` findings against that file before, **zero** after.

## 2 — Two locus footguns, now guarded

Both bit this session.

**`number-stranded` had no locus guard.** Its header said *"run in the checkout carrying the stray"* — and a lane carries it too, but the NNN it assigns is only valid against serialized main (#2288). Assigned in a lane, `check:standards` rejects the result from the other side (*"a hand-picked NNN not on origin/main"*). So the verb refused **both ways at once** and left a half-applied rename with no verb to finish it — 7 cards renamed, then reverted by hand. It now refuses in a lane and names where it does belong.

**Lane auto-pick could return the caller's own lane**, and acquiring resets to the integration branch — so a bare `acquire --purpose=review-juror` returned the driving lane and reset its checkout mid-task.

Scoped deliberately: **this is not the data-loss guard.** `isLaneAcquirable`'s `dirtyOrAhead` test (#2267) already refuses a lane holding uncommitted or unpushed work, and it *held* in that incident — nothing was lost, only checkout state. This is the narrower surprise of a clean, pushed lane being reset while its owner is still in it. A preference, not a refusal: `--lane=N` is honoured as asked, and a single-lane pool still acquires its only lane.

## 3 — The habit behind them, as memory

Five mistakes this session looked unrelated. They were one thing: **acting from a plausible assumption where a cheap authoritative check existed.**

| Asserted | The check would have said |
|---|---|
| "the operations can't be used on a VM" | `docs/agent/vm-sessions.md:88` documents the arc; the review skill documents the transport 60 lines below where reading stopped |
| "11 skill lines instruct raw homes" | the scan matches an *invocation*, not a mention — real count **0** |
| "#3321/#3214 are resolved over open work" | #3214 is a ratified *decision*; #3321 is a story and the guard is epic-only — both correct by design |
| "`number-stranded` fixes this" | it must run on main; the error said "run X" without a locus |
| used raw `backlog.mjs resolve` ×25 | the declared operation exists and owns four guards |
| "#1961 needs the operator's review" | the rubric answers exactly that: `humanRequired: false` — an *independent* review is owed, not a human one |

Recorded as `agent-memory-src/verify-before-asserting-the-tree.md`, indexed under `index-verif`. No gate catches "reported a grep count as a finding" or "forwarded an unverified claim" — the instances differ every time, the habit is the constant.

## 4 — #xkomby1: the review skill's VM write-path gap

Filed, not fixed. The skill documents the VM **read** path thoroughly and says nothing about the **write** path, which fails on the same host: `advisory-note` and `label-swap` both call `gh`. Three things a reviewer then needs live only in `vm-sessions.md` or nowhere — resolving an UNKNOWN-outcome effect, transcribing the juror's findings when `advisory-note` fails, and disclosing that a connector label swap bypassed the single home. Not a duplicate of #3267, which fixes the mechanism rather than the map.

## 5 — Binding the Bash guard to `DECLARED_HOMES`

Two hook gaps, both the same shape as #3224: the mechanism knew a **raw home** and not the **operation declaring over it**.

**Backgrounded verification, operation form.** `VERIFICATION_RUN` anchors on `verify-lane.mjs` / `check:standards` / `test:unit`, so `run.mjs verify` — which shells `verify-lane` through `verify-io` — was invisible to it. Backgrounding that is the #2833 stall exactly as backgrounding the home is, and it was measured the day this landed: **four backgrounded `run.mjs verify` calls in one session, two of which returned `unrun` and were nearly reported green.**

The operation list is **derived from `DECLARED_HOMES`**, never hand-listed, for the reason that map's own header gives — a second list of the same relationship drifts from the moment it is written. An operation declaring over a guarded home is covered the day it is declared.

**A truncating pipe on an operation's `--json`.** `--json` emits the whole payload, so it overflows a terminal and invites a `| tail -N`. That does not truncate a *view*, it corrupts the *value*: the JSON stops parsing, so the verdict is lost **entirely** rather than partially. Three times in one session; twice recovered only from the durable run record. The denial names both free remedies — drop `--json` for the compact render, or redirect to a file to parse it — plus `.operations/runs/`, which survives whatever happens to stdout.

Both predicates are anchored to the runner **plus** script path, as `VERIFICATION_RUN` is, so a mention is not a run. That anchoring was missing on the first cut of the BACKGROUNDING predicate and **a new test caught it**: `echo "run.mjs verify …"` matched as a verification run — the same mention-vs-invocation error this PR corrects elsewhere.

> **Corrected in `9426841c` (review round 3).** As first written this paragraph was true of the backgrounding predicate and **false of the truncation one**, which carried no runner anchor at all — so `echo "run.mjs verify --json" | tail -5` was denied as if it were the command. Reviewing the confirmed finding below turned up two further defects in that same regex: it also denied a safe `--json > file` followed by an unrelated `| tail` in a *later statement* (the juror's finding), and it **allowed** `--json | jq . | tail -5`, walking straight past the exact corruption it exists to stop, because an intervening `|` broke its `[^|]*` run. All three are fixed by scoping the predicate through `parseSegments`' `pipedFrom` — one pipeline, not one string — and pinned by five cases that redden when the old regex is restored. The sentence above is now true of both predicates rather than withdrawn.

## 6 — #xjdwz4z: a lane verify marker outlives its landed PR

Filed, not fixed. `verify-lane` writes a terminal green to `.git/.lane-verify` and refuses to overwrite it — correct — but nothing clears it when the PR it certified **lands**, so the lane becomes permanently unverifiable. `lane-1`'s marker held green for `ef74eb85` (#1959, merged 19:42) and refused to verify the next change in the same lane. Cleared by hand after proving the sha is an ancestor of `origin/main` — the right test in the wrong place. The card proposes moving exactly that check into the refusal. **It bit a second time in this PR** (marker red for `63924c84`, a strict ancestor of the head whose recorded failure the head had already fixed), cleared the same way — the same proof the card wants moved into the refusal.

## 7 — #3531: the leverage test raced a live directory

The card's diagnosis was cross-file `WE_VISUAL_FIXTURES` pollution, and it is **falsified**: `src/_data/backlog.js` resolves `BACKLOG_DIR` once at module load and reads neither clock nor env on the leverage path, so after the `require` no env mutation can move those fields. There is no polluter to name. The four fields are a pure function of the `backlog/*.md` corpus, and the test read that corpus **twice, seconds apart, from a live directory** that scaffold/resolve/the drain write to. `frozen-backlog.ts` copies the corpus per file and points the loader at the copy; the determinism assertion is untouched. `frozen-backlog.test.ts` pins the hazard, the falsification, the control, exact env restoration, and the wiring (mutating the call site reddens two cases).

## Verification

- `run.mjs verify` — **"verified green for `9426841c`"**, no blocking findings, run in the foreground.
- `npx vitest run` **unsharded** — 412 files, **10,837 passing**, exit 0. `npm run check:standards` — **0 errors**.
- Review round 3: an independent juror panel (correctness + security) reduced to **`accept`**, `humanRequired: false`, converged at round 1. Its one finding was confirmed against the running code and fixed in `9426841c` rather than accepted over.

## Transport note

Planned by `run.mjs open-pr` (`--ref=lane/xzitlr9-dispatcher-operations --mode=park --parkLabel=review:pending --sha=ef249622 --require-verified`), which halted at `submit` because this host has no `gh` credential and instructed submitting the planned argv through a channel that has one. Only the transport differs from the operation's plan. The `review:pending` park label needs applying as a second call, and — per `vm-sessions.md` — a label applied that way is **unguarded by construction**: `pr-land.mjs#withAuthorStamp` never ran, so there is no `authored-by-actor` stamp and the `STAMP_LOST` self-clear refusal cannot fire. #3267 is the fix.

**This body edit likewise bypassed its single home.** `scripts/pr-body-edit.mjs` shells `gh`, which this host does not have, so the edit went through the connector — the same disclosure #xkomby1 says the skill should require and does not.

## Review round 2 — one finding, fixed; and a base-branch red that is not this PR's

### Panel, round 2 (head `5a7cd356`)

`security: accept` (no findings) · `correctness: prevention-outstanding` — down from 3 findings to **1**, and the same class as before: `numberStranded`'s lane refusal was *wired* but only the extracted predicate was tested, so a call site that failed to invoke it would still ship a guard that never fires.

Round 1 fixed that finding **by half**, and my commit message claimed it whole. Fixed properly in `f8ae8bc8`:

- `scripts/__tests__/number-stranded-locus.test.mjs` spawns the real CLI with a synthesised `<tmp>/.lanes/<pool>/lane-1` cwd — not the lane the suite happens to run in, since the assertion must hold in CI where the checkout is not a lane — and asserts the refusal plus both remedies it names.
- **Mutation-proven, not asserted:** guarding the call site with `false &&` reddens the test; restoring it greens.
- A second case pins that the guard does *not* fire outside a lane, so it cannot regress into refusing everywhere.

### `verify-lane` is red, and the cause is #3531

The marker records red on `63924c84`. The failure is a single test:

```
FAIL src/_data/__tests__/backlog-leverage.test.ts
  > backlog unblock-leverage — derivation invariants
  > is deterministic — a second load produces identical leverage fields
```

That is **#3531**, filed against `main` a few minutes before this run, whose own body reads: *"`npx vitest run` (no shard) fails on `main` today"* and names this exact test. It passes standalone (7/7) and fails only at full-suite size — order-dependence pre-existing on the base branch. This PR adds a test file, which shifts suite ordering and *surfaces* it; it does not cause it.

Evidence it is not this diff:
- `npm run test:unit` standalone: **411 files, 10,814 passing**, exit 0.
- `npm run check:standards` standalone: **0 errors**.
- The failing test passes in isolation; only the unsharded full-suite run reddens.
- CI shards, which is precisely why #3531 says CI cannot see this.

No fix exists to port — #3531 was only just filed. Per the drive-to-green rules this is the one legitimate "not mine", and this comment is the required standing-down note rather than silence.

### Also merged

`origin/main` at `885352b5` merged in, which brought the drain's `number-stranded` sweep (the 3 hash cards that made an earlier verify red have since been numbered #3531–#3533). That earlier red *was* transient base-branch strandedness and has self-healed; this one has not.

### State

- Functionally green: 10,824 passing, `check:standards` 0 errors, both halves clean standalone.
- `verify-lane` marker red on the #3531 failure, so the finish-guard will refuse to land — correctly, since it cannot tell whose failure it is.
- Landing waits on #3531, or on a decision to land past a known base-branch red.

## #3531 is fixed in this PR — standing-down note above is withdrawn

I said this PR couldn't land until #3531 was fixed on `main`. It's fixed here instead, in `e0bc4d2b`, because the fix turned out to be three files and no base-branch change.

**The card's diagnosis was wrong, and I could falsify it executably.** The leading hypothesis was cross-file `WE_VISUAL_FIXTURES` pollution from a sibling test. But `src/_data/backlog.js` resolves `BACKLOG_DIR` **once, at module load**, holds no module-level cache, and reads neither the clock nor the environment on the leverage path. So after the `require`, no env mutation by any file can move `directUnblocks` / `transitiveUnblocks` / `unblocksToReady` / `leverageScore`. Flipping both `WE_VISUAL_FIXTURES` and `WE_BACKLOG_DIR` between the two loads leaves them **identical**. There is no polluting test to name.

That leaves exactly one reachable cause, and it isn't order dependence:

| probe | result |
| --- | --- |
| flip `WE_VISUAL_FIXTURES` **and** `WE_BACKLOG_DIR` between the two loads | identical — env cannot reach these fields |
| write one card into the corpus between the two loads | **differ**, by the exact expected delta (`001:1:1:1:1001` → `001:2:2:2:2002`) |
| change nothing between the two loads | identical — the derivation itself was never at fault |

The four fields are a pure function of the `backlog/*.md` corpus, and the test read that corpus **twice, seconds apart, from a live directory** that `scaffold`, `resolve` and the drain write to. Any write landing between the two reads reddens it. Small runs put the reads milliseconds apart and nothing lands; the full run widens the window until something does — which is precisely the card's own probe table (the file alone passes, every subset passes, only the full run fails), with no worker-packing story needed.

**The fix is at the isolation seam; the determinism assertion is untouched.** `frozen-backlog.ts` copies the corpus to a temp dir once per file and points the loader at the copy via `WE_BACKLOG_DIR`, restoring the variable immediately after the `require` — it only has to survive that one call — so the file leaves no `process.env` residue for whatever vitest packs in next. The claim keeps its full force: the same derivation, run twice, over the real 3500-card corpus, no longer racing a directory other processes own.

`frozen-backlog.test.ts` pins the hazard, the falsification, the control, the helper's immutability and its exact env restoration (including the was-unset case, which a naive save/restore turns into an empty string) — and the **wiring**. Testing a helper is not testing that the leverage test calls it: mutating the call site back to a bare `require` reddens two cases. Verified by mutation, not asserted.

**The CI blind spot, stated on the card:** CI could never have caught this, and sharding is not the reason — a CI checkout has no concurrent writer to `backlog/`, so the race has no second party there. Sharding is a real but *separate* blind spot for order dependence generally, and it is accepted: an unsharded gate costs the `test` lane its wall-clock budget, and this isolation fix means the defect can no longer occur at any file count, in or out of CI.

**Verification on this head:** `npx vitest run` unsharded — 412 files, **10,837 passing**, exit 0. `npm run check:standards` — **0 errors**. #3531 resolved through `run.mjs resolve`.
